findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration indexes the result of the embed_category lookup without any empty-result guard (`WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`), so on any install where the `embed_category` site_setting row does not exist (all fresh installs, and any upgrade where the setting was never changed from its '' default — Discourse only persists non-default settings) `execute(...)[0]` yields no row and the migration raises instead of completing. Fresh installs and upgrades without embed_category set fail to run migrations and cannot boot; the fallback `if category_id == 0` branch is unreachable because the crash happens on the lookup line first. Note the same migration guards the embeddable_hosts query with `cmd_tuples > 0` but omits the guard here — the asymmetry confirms the edge case was considered and dropped for this query.

[BUG] The migration inserts the raw setting values verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host without the normalization the model applies (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//,'')` and path stripping run only in before_validation, which raw SQL bypasses), but the new lookup `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host` — so any setting entry stored with an `http://`/`https://` prefix or a path (formats the old setting explicitly supported and the old `allows_embeddable_host?` normalized at comparison time, per the deleted spec cases `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = 'http://eviltrout.com'`) is migrated in a form that can never match a referer hostname. Every site that had hosts configured with a protocol prefix or path silently loses embedding on upgrade: `ensure_embeddable` raises Discourse::InvalidAccess for those referers and `topic_retriever` drops imports as invalid_host?, with no error surfaced to the admin — the admin UI shows the host rows as present and valid-looking.

[BUG] Both `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check, so a request for a nonexistent/deleted id calls `save_host(nil)` → `nil.host=` or `nil.destroy` and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any stale client state (two admin tabs, a delete confirmed after another admin deleted the row, a retry after a failed save) produces a 500 error dialog via popupAjaxError instead of a graceful 'record not found' response; the destroy path also skips the destroyRecord failure handling on the client because the server 500s before success_json.

[BUG] The diff wires `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` and `this.store.find('embedding')` but adds no model definition for either type (no models/embedding.* or models/embeddable-host.* anywhere in the diff), while the custom Discourse store resolves the model class via the container for createRecord and for hydrating `category_id` back into `host.category` (the component reads `host.get('category.id')` and `buffered.host`). Loading /admin/customize/embedding or clicking 'Add Host' fails because the store has no model class for 'embedding'/'embeddable-host' — the admin screen the feature is named for cannot be exercised at all; the new adapter and the ADMIN_MODELS/rest.js plumbing added in this same diff have no model to serve.

[BUG] The spec added for the controller that carries all the new persistence behavior (save_host with the blank-category→uncategorized fallback, validation failure → render_json_error, update/destroy) contains only one assertion — that the class is a subclass of AdminController — and the sibling embedding_controller_spec.rb is identical; no assertion anywhere in the diff covers create/update/destroy request handling. A regression in save_host (e.g. the category_id blank fallback, or the 500-on-missing-id behavior above) ships green; the only 'verification' for the feature's write path is a class-hierarchy check, which is why the nil-host crash in the controller is uncaught.

[ADVISORY] `EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op — it re-renders the serializer without persisting anything — and the paired client action `saveChanges()` calls `embedding.update({})`, so the PUT /customize/embedding route added in config/routes.rb is a dead endpoint on both sides. Any future contributor or plugin wiring a save button to saveChanges gets a success response with zero effect (silent data loss for the user); today it is ships-inert code — either delete the action/route or make update persist, since the current 'save' story is entirely per-host via EmbeddableHostsController.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation on `host`, so the admin UI (which creates a fresh record per 'Add Host') happily saves duplicate rows for the same host with different categories, and `record_for_host` resolves the conflict with `.first` on an unordered `where("lower(host) = ?")` query. When two rows share a host, embedded topics are filed into an arbitrary one of their categories (nondeterministic with no ORDER BY), and the admin has no signal in the UI that a duplicate exists; add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) or a unique index in the migration.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator contents were swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category definitions. The code works because all fabricator files are loaded, but the next contributor editing 'category_fabricator.rb' finds the embeddable-host fabricator there, and grepping the fabricator tree for the category fabricators points at the wrong file — rename the files to match their contents before this ossifies.

[ADVISORY] The INSERT statement interpolates the stored setting value directly: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ..."` with no quoting/escaping of `h`. Any legacy embeddable_hosts entry containing a single quote (admin free-text in a site setting) makes the INSERT raise and aborts the migration mid-apply, leaving the deploy stuck; use `insert`/parameterized SQL or the model instead of string interpolation.

[BUG] The migration crashes on any install where the site_settings table has no 'embed_category' row, because execute(...)[0]['id'] is called on an empty result (PG::Result raises IndexError for an out-of-range index, or nil['id'] raises NoMethodError). Fresh installs and upgrades where the admin never changed embed_category from its default (the default is never persisted to site_settings) fail db:migrate entirely, blocking setup/upgrade at this migration.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim without applying the model's normalization (scheme/path stripping in EmbeddableHost's before_validation), so values like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'example.com/1234' — both of which the old setting supported per the removed site_setting_spec cases — are stored unnormalized. After upgrade, EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares uri.host against the stored string and never matches these rows, so sites whose old setting used scheme- or path-form entries silently lose embedding (comments/embed actions raise InvalidAccess) with no error surfaced to the admin.

[BUG] update passes a nil host into save_host when no EmbeddableHost exists for params[:id], so host.host= raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. A stale admin tab (host deleted in another session) submitting an edit gets a 500 with a raw exception instead of a meaningful 'not found' response.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record when the id does not exist, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Double-delete of the same host (e.g. retry after a timeout) produces a 500 instead of idempotent success or a 404.

[BUG] before_validation calls self.host.sub! on a possibly-nil host, so creating an EmbeddableHost with a nil host param raises NoMethodError before the format validation can reject it. A POST/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts omitting embeddable_host[host] (or params[:embeddable_host] entirely) returns a 500 instead of the 422 validation error the serializer contract implies.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint persists nothing — update just re-renders the serialized embedding — and its only client caller, saveChanges in admin-embedding.js.es6, is never invoked by any template in this diff. Ships an inert staff-writable endpoint plus dead client action and OpenStruct aggregate ('embedding' wrapper) that adds three files of surface for zero behavior; a future maintainer must reason about (or secure) an endpoint that does nothing — the hosts CRUD alone already fully serves the stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] The contents of category_fabricator.rb and the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines all four category fabricators. All fabricators still register (Fabrication keys by name, not file), but anyone editing category fixtures will open embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa, and git history for category fabricators now points at the wrong file — a comprehension/change-safety trap planted by this diff.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the 'embedding is configured' condition entirely (previously SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?) instead of replacing it with an EmbeddableHost-existence check. The invariant 'first post is expandable only when embedding is set up' is no longer enforced: a site that deletes all its hosts (or has orphaned TopicEmbed rows with no hosts) now shows the expandable-first-post UI for embedded topics, a behavior change not traceable to the admin-editing requirement.

[ADVISORY] Unrelated test-only cleanup (removing unused 'topic' local variables in the for_digest muted-category and TL0 specs) is bundled into this feature diff. Reviewers and future bisects must treat these digest-spec changes as part of the embedding feature; if either spec's behavior changes later, blame history attributes it to this PR though nothing in the feature touched it.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host compares against uri.host (which never contains a port), but the validation regex on line 2 explicitly permits a ':[0-9]{1,5}' port suffix, so a host saved as 'example.com:8080' can never match any referer. An admin who enters a host with a port — input the form accepts and serializes without complaint — gets a row that silently whitelists nothing; embedding from that host keeps failing with no diagnostic.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex requires a dotted TLD of 2-5 letters, rejecting hostnames the previous setting-based system accepted, such as 'localhost' or intranet names without a dot. Installs that relied on whitelisting 'localhost' or internal hostnames via the old embeddable_hosts setting cannot re-create that configuration after upgrading; their embed setup is unrecoverable through the new UI.

[ADVISORY] The migration's non-trivial data-transfer logic (category lookup by name join, uncategorized fallback, host-row seeding) has no test anywhere in this diff. A regression in the settings-to-table backfill would corrupt or drop every existing site's embedding configuration with nothing failing in CI; this is the highest-blast-risk code in the PR and the least covered.

[ADVISORY] The spec for the new controller asserts only the AdminController subclass relationship; none of the save_host behavior (blank category_id defaulting to uncategorized, error rendering, update path) is exercised. The blank-category defaulting rule — a real behavioral requirement echoed in the migration — is enforced by zero tests, so a regression that drops the default would silently create hosts with no category routing for embedded topics.

[BUG] PUT /admin/customize/embedding is an advertised route whose update action only re-renders the serializer and persists nothing, yet returns 200 success. Any caller of the update endpoint — including the client's admin-embedding controller whose saveChanges() invokes embedding.update({}) which PUTs to exactly this route — receives a success response while no data is written; a caller relying on this endpoint to persist embedding configuration silently loses its changes with no error signal.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com', 'https://example.com/1234' — forms the old setting and its specs accepted) while the runtime lookup EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) = uri.host, i.e. bare lowercase hostname. After upgrade, every migrated host row that carries a scheme or path never matches the lookup, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? returns false for previously-working referers and ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess — embedded comments break site-wide for those hosts with no error surfaced to the admin, because the model's before_validation normalization is bypassed by the raw SQL insert.

[BUG] record_for_host compares the port-stripped uri.host against the stored host column, but the format validation on line 2 explicitly permits a ':[0-9]{1,5}' port suffix and before_validation never strips it, so the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form. An admin saves 'example.com:8080' (passes validation), but every lookup uses uri.host = 'example.com', so lower(host) = ? can never match; the host appears configured in the admin UI yet host_allowed? permanently returns false and embedded comments for that host are denied with InvalidAccess.

[BUG] The host format regex requires a final-label TLD of 2–5 letters (\.[a-z]{2,5}) and a dot at all, so valid modern-TLD hosts and 'localhost' are rejected by the model validation. An admin cannot add legitimate hosts like 'example.technology', 'example.online', or 'myforum.construction' — save fails with a validation error — even though these are exactly the hostnames the feature is meant to allowlist; the schema encodes a 2012-era TLD assumption as a hard business rule.

[ADVISORY] The embed allowlist check moved from an in-memory cached SiteSetting to an unconditional per-request DB query (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? -> where(lower(host) = ?)) on the public, unauthenticated, high-traffic /embed/comments path, and the LOWER(host) predicate is non-sargable so no index on host can serve it. Every comment-iframe request from every embedded site now costs a full-table scan on embeddable_hosts; a site with heavy embedding traffic pays a DB roundtrip per request where the previous design served the answer from the cached settings object, and the table will grow one row per host with no caching layer to absorb it.

[ADVISORY] belongs_to :category has no foreign key in the migration, no null-guard, and no dependent cleanup, so embeddable_hosts rows can outlive their category. When an admin deletes the category a host points at, the row survives with a dangling category_id; TopicEmbed.import then passes the dead id to PostCreator as category:, and topic creation for that host fails on every subsequent embedded import until someone notices and re-edits the host.

[ADVISORY] The contents of category_fabricator.rb and the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines all the category fabricators. Both files load so tests still pass, but the next contributor who opens category_fabricator.rb to change category fixtures edits the wrong file and finds no category fabricator there — a guaranteed future mis-edit and comprehension trap baked into the repo.

[ADVISORY] update and destroy call .first on the id lookup and use the result with no nil guard: save_host(nil) raises NoMethodError on host.host=, and destroy calls nil.destroy. PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id (e.g. a second admin already deleted the host) returns a 500 from NoMethodError instead of the 404 the REST contract promises, surfacing as an ajax error popup blaming the acting admin.

[ADVISORY] before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no presence validation on host, so a nil host raises NoMethodError inside the callback instead of producing a validation error. EmbeddableHost.new.save — reachable via any client that omits the host param — crashes with a 500 rather than the 4xx render_json_error path the controller builds for validation failures, and the null: false column constraint is the only remaining guard, which the callback defeats by erroring first.

[ADVISORY] The public singleton method SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? is deleted outright with no deprecation shim, changing the public surface of a widely-extended class. Out-of-tree plugins or themes that call SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? (a natural integration point for host filtering) fail with NoMethodError after upgrade, with the only notice being a one-line removal in server.en.yml's neighborhood — no log message, no graceful migration path.

[ADVISORY] The new plural id-list hydration branch lacks the guard the singular branch has: singular checks `if (hydrated)` before assigning and deleting the key, but the plural branch assigns obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated.map(...) unconditionally, embedding undefined entries when an id is not found by _lookupSubType. A payload listing a related id whose record is not side-loaded in the root produces an array containing undefined; every consumer that iterates the hydrated collection (e.g. the admin embedding template's {{#each embedding.embeddable_hosts}}) hits undefined property access during render, and the asymmetry with the guarded singular branch guarantees the next editor of one branch misses the other.

[BUG] The review iteration silently removed the development-mode admin bypass: the old code skipped the host check when `Rails.env.development? && current_user.try(:admin?)`, but the new code raises Discourse::InvalidAccess unconditionally unless the referer matches an EmbeddableHost row. A developer running a local Discourse in development mode as admin can no longer test embedding from any referer; embed pages now 403/redirect until they manually insert an EmbeddableHost row for their local hostname — a behavior regression nobody accepted in review.

[BUG] The `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard was dropped from `expandable_first_post?` without a replacement (no `EmbeddableHost.exists?` check), so the method now returns true based solely on `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. On a site where all EmbeddableHost rows are deleted (or a fresh install that previously used topic embeds), first posts of topic-embedded topics remain expandable even though embedding is no longer permitted — the old setting presence acted as a kill-switch that this iteration deleted without human sign-off.

[BUG] The migration interpolates the raw `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value directly into SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), with no escaping and no validation applied at this point. Any pre-existing setting value containing a single quote (or other SQL-significant character) raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and aborts the migration mid-flight, blocking the site's upgrade; because rows are inserted one-by-one without a transaction wrapper, a partial import can also be left behind.

[BUG] The migration copies host values verbatim from the old setting, but the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` prefixes before matching while the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored string with exact equality against `uri.host`. Sites whose `embeddable_hosts` setting contained scheme-prefixed entries (a form the old matcher explicitly supported, per the deleted 'works with a http host' spec) get rows stored as `https://example.com`, which never equal `example.com` — their embedding silently stops working after upgrade with no error surfaced.

[BUG] `update` and `destroy` look up the host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then dereference it without a nil check, so a stale or bogus id passes `host` as nil into `save_host`/`destroy`. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/<bad-id> crashes with NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of the 404 the REST contract implies; a stale Ember record (deleted in another tab) turns an admin's delete click into a 500 error popup via popupAjaxError.

[BUG] The new fabricator file contains only the relocated `:category`/`:diff_category`/`:happy_category`/`:private_category` definitions; no `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` block exists anywhere in this diff, yet embed_controller_spec, embeddable_host_spec, topic_embed_spec and topic_spec all call `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)`. Every new and modified spec raises Fabrication::UnknownFabricatorError ('No such factory: embeddable_host'), so the server test suite fails wholesale — the iteration that moved the category fabricators into this file lost the factory the feature's own tests depend on.

[ADVISORY] The public `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` method and the `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings are removed outright with no deprecation shim, while `type: host_list` disappears from site_settings.yml. Any out-of-tree plugin or theme calling `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` (a documented-ish extension point) breaks with NoMethodError on upgrade instead of getting a graceful false/deprecation warning; the old body also contained an unreachable second matching block that is deleted without comment, so this historical behavior quirk is undocumented anywhere.

[ADVISORY] The `_hydrateEmbedded` regex broadened from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`, so every existing payload key matching `*_ids` — which previously passed through untouched as a raw id array on the record — is now intercepted, hydrated via `_lookupSubType`, moved to the pluralized key, and the raw `*_ids` key is deleted. Any existing client code reading `record.get('some_ids')` on a serialized payload silently gets hydrated model objects (or an empty array) instead of ids after this change; the change was introduced for the embedding feature's `embeddable_host_ids` but rewrites hydration behavior for the entire store, a coupling the PR title does not surface.

[ADVISORY] The `update` action (wired to PUT /customize/embedding and called by the client's `saveChanges()` via `embedding.update({})`) performs no persistence at all — it just re-serializes the fetched OpenStruct and renders success. The route and the `saveChanges` controller action are a dead/inert pair: the embedding.hbs template has no save button today, and the next maintainer who wires one up gets a request that reports success while saving nothing, a silent no-op masquerading as a working endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The test still named 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer exercises a blank-host scenario: no host is fabricated, but `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` is also left at its false default, so the assertion passes trivially via the truncate condition. The removed `embeddable_hosts.present?` guard in `expandable_first_post?` is now invisible to the suite — a regression that resurrects or further alters that guard's semantics cannot be caught by this test, and the test name actively misleads future readers about what is covered.

[ADVISORY] The validation regex accepts a host with a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`, and URI#host never includes a port. An admin who legitimately saves `example.com:8080` (accepted by the validator) creates a row that can never match any referer, so the host is silently inert — the admin believes embedding from that host works while every embed request still raises InvalidAccess.

[BUG] The data migration interpolates the admin-configured embeddable_hosts setting value directly into a raw SQL INSERT: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)", so any single quote or backslash in a stored host string is executed as SQL. An attacker (or a merely careless admin) who set SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts to a value containing a quote before this migration runs — e.g. "x'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts;--" or "a','b'); UPDATE site_settings ..." — gets arbitrary SQL executed against the production database at deploy time; the migration is the config-backed sink and no escaping or parameterization is applied to #{h}.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten ensure_embeddable gate authorizes the /embed/comments endpoint solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)), which any HTTP client can set to an allowlisted value. Any unauthenticated party who learns one allowlisted host (they are enumerable via scraped embeds) can forge Referer: http://that-host and consume the embed endpoint server-side, using the forum as a scraped/relayable content source; the control is a policy check on a spoofable header, not an authentication boundary. This weakness is inherited from the replaced SiteSetting check, but the diff rewrites the exact lines enforcing it and cements the header as the sole gate.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host normalizes the incoming referer via URI parsing (which strips port and lowercases) but compares it against the stored host column verbatim, while the validation regex explicitly permits stored hosts with a port suffix (:\\d{1,5}) — a normalization mismatch between what is stored and what is queried. An admin who follows the UI precedent of entering a host with a port (the regex advertises it as valid) stores 'eviltrout.com:8080', which lower(host) = 'eviltrout.com' can never match; the admin silently gets no embedding anywhere (fail-closed, so no spoofing bypass, but the stored-vs-queried canonical forms drift and the admin cannot discover why without reading source). A functional index or downcasing/port-stripping on save would make stored and queried forms identical.

[BUG] The rewritten test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes for the wrong reason: it runs with no before-block, so SiteSetting.embed_truncate is still its default false (config/site_settings.yml line 'embed_truncate: false'), meaning expandable_first_post? returns false via the truncate check and the embeddable-host condition is never exercised. The test passes whether or not the code consults embeddable hosts at all — and indeed the new code (topic.rb line 869) removed the host check entirely, so the test name now describes behavior that no longer exists; a regression that re-adds or misimplements host gating (or drops truncate gating) would not be caught, and no test in the diff demonstrates the actual new behavior (true when embed_truncate? and has_topic_embed? hold with zero hosts fabricated).

[ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts the class hierarchy (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`) and never exercises create, update, or destroy. The new controller logic — params[:embeddable_host][:host]/[:category_id] extraction, the blank-category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 27-28), validation-failure rendering, and destroy of a nil host (line 17: `nil.destroy` raises NoMethodError when params[:id] doesn't match) — ships with zero behavioral assertions; any of these regressions passes CI green.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddingController is a subclass check; neither show nor update is ever requested, and the update action's behavior (re-rendering the serializer with no persistence — embedding_controller.rb lines 11-13) is unverified. The admin embedding page's entire load path (OpenStruct model, EmbeddingSerializer with embed: :ids producing embeddable_host_ids that the new plural hydration in store.js must consume) and the saveChanges PUT round-trip have no test; a serializer key rename or route change passes CI and breaks the admin UI at runtime.

[ADVISORY] The pretender handler for GET /fruits/:id returns a hard-coded `fruits[0]` regardless of the requested id, and the store-test change to `store.find('fruit', 2)` (store-test.js.es6 lines 109-124) then asserts color ids 1,2 — which are apple's (fruits[0]) data, not banana's (color_ids [3]) — and never asserts `f.get('id')`. The switch from find('fruit', 1) to find('fruit', 2) is decorative: the fixture ignores the id, so the test cannot detect a hydration/identity-map bug that attaches the wrong record or wrong embedded children for a non-first record; any per-id lookup regression in store.js passes while the test appears to cover a second record.

[ADVISORY] The host_allowed? specs only use exact lowercase, port-free fixtures, while the validation regex on EmbeddableHost (embeddable_host.rb line 5) accepts hosts with a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and uppercase (//i), and before_validation strips neither ports nor case — but record_for_host compares `lower(host) = uri.host` (line 15), which excludes the port and is downcased. A host saved as 'Example.com:8080' or 'Example.com' passes validation and is persisted, yet host_allowed? can never match it ('example.com' ≠ 'example.com:8080' / stored case is not downcased before comparison), so the admin successfully adds a host that silently never allows embedding; the spec's fixture set (eviltrout.com, discourse.org) is exactly the input shape where this mismatch is invisible, so the defect ships covered-green.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category definitions. Tests still pass because Fabricate resolves by name across all fabricator files, but the file names now lie about their contents — the next contributor adding a category fabricator trait to category_fabricator.rb or a second embeddable_host definition (duplicate Fabricator name raises at load) gets bitten; this reads as a rename/move accident rather than intent.

[BUG] The guard `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is always false for a SELECT in PostgreSQL (PQcmdTuples returns 0 for SELECT statements), so the guarded INSERT block never runs, while the following `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` executes unconditionally. Every existing site's configured embeddable hosts are silently destroyed from site_settings with zero rows created in embeddable_hosts; after deploy, EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? returns false for all referers, breaking embedding site-wide (embed_controller/topic_retriever now depend on the table), and admins have no record of what hosts they had configured to re-enter.

[BUG] `execute(...)[0]['id']` and `execute(...)[0]['value']` are indexed without a presence check, so when the first query returns no rows (embed_category setting absent, or its value not matching any category name exactly — e.g. the category was renamed or the setting stored an id), `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError instead of reaching the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback that was written for exactly this case. The migration crashes mid-run on affected installs (table already created, transaction not clean), blocking the deploy; and because the CREATE TABLE is not recorded, any re-run hits the force: true drop path. The uncategorized fallback branch at lines 13-15 is dead code — the crash always happens first when the join is empty.

[BUG] Host values from the free-text site_settings row are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no escaping or parameterization, so any previously configured host containing a single quote or other SQL-significant character produces a malformed statement. The migration raises a PG syntax error mid-migration (deploy blocker), aborting after the table has been created; even without quotes, the raw interpolation skips the escaping/parameterization the model layer would have applied. (Injection is Security's angle; the migration-crash data-integrity failure is this one.)

[BUG] The backfill INSERT bypasses the model's before_validation callback: raw setting values are stored as-is, so hosts saved with a protocol or path prefix (the old setting explicitly documented and accepted forms like 'http://discourse.org/1234' — see the removed embed_controller_spec fixtures) land in the host column unnormalized. Even once the cmd_tuples guard bug is fixed, every migrated host row containing 'http://' or a trailing path never matches `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, so the migrated hosts silently fail to allow embedding while appearing in the admin UI as if configured; a later admin edit of such a row would also fail the validates_format_of regex since the protocol was never stripped.

[BUG] The migration is defined with `def change` but contains raw `execute` INSERT and DELETE statements that ActiveRecord cannot reverse, so `db:rollback` raises IrreversibleMigration, and the DELETE of the site_settings rows ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') destroys those values with no backup/export step. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The validation regex accepts a host with a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) but `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`, and URI#host never includes a port. An admin who legitimately saves `example.com:8080` (accepted by the validator) creates a row that can never match any referer, so the host is silently inert — the admin believes embedding from that host works while every embed request still raises InvalidAccess.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port suffix `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), and the `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not strip `:port`, so `example.com:8080` can be persisted. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`; `URI#host` returns only the hostname without the port. Therefore a stored row containing a port will never match any referer/embed URL, making the configured host silently ineffective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The data migration interpolates the admin-configured embeddable_hosts setting value directly into a raw SQL INSERT: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)", so any single quote or backslash in a stored host string is executed as SQL. An attacker (or a merely careless admin) who set SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts to a value containing a quote before this migration runs — e.g. "x'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts;--" or "a','b'); UPDATE site_settings ..." — gets arbitrary SQL executed against the production database at deploy time; the migration is the config-backed sink and no escaping or parameterization is applied to #{h}.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the prior SiteSetting 'embeddable_hosts' value from the DB, splits it, and then performs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` for each entry. `h` is interpolated directly into raw SQL without quoting/escaping or parameterization, so a value containing a single quote can break the SQL and could be leveraged for SQL injection during migration execution (at minimum, it can cause deploy-time migration failure/data corruption).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten ensure_embeddable gate authorizes the /embed/comments endpoint solely on the client-supplied Referer header (EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)), which any HTTP client can set to an allowlisted value. Any unauthenticated party who learns one allowlisted host (they are enumerable via scraped embeds) can forge Referer: http://that-host and consume the embed endpoint server-side, using the forum as a scraped/relayable content source; the control is a policy check on a spoofable header, not an authentication boundary. This weakness is inherited from the replaced SiteSetting check, but the diff rewrites the exact lines enforcing it and cements the header as the sole gate.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the only runtime gate shown in the diff for non-dev/non-admin requests is `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (and `record_for_host` parses the passed string via `URI(...)`). This is indeed entirely based on the client-supplied `Referer` header, which an HTTP client can forge. However, the diff itself also shows this is largely a refactor of the prior behavior (previously `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` also used `request.referer`), so it’s not clearly a newly introduced, verifiable defect vs. an existing design/policy limitation. It’s a concrete, diff-grounded security/architecture concern worth flagging, but not provably an unintended bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] record_for_host normalizes the incoming referer via URI parsing (which strips port and lowercases) but compares it against the stored host column verbatim, while the validation regex explicitly permits stored hosts with a port suffix (:\\d{1,5}) — a normalization mismatch between what is stored and what is queried. An admin who follows the UI precedent of entering a host with a port (the regex advertises it as valid) stores 'eviltrout.com:8080', which lower(host) = 'eviltrout.com' can never match; the admin silently gets no embedding anywhere (fail-closed, so no spoofing bypass, but the stored-vs-queried canonical forms drift and the admin cannot discover why without reading source). A functional index or downcasing/port-stripping on save would make stored and queried forms identical.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost, `before_validation` strips scheme and path but leaves any port intact (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), and the validation regex explicitly allows a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and uses `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. So a stored value like `eviltrout.com:8080` can never match an incoming referer like `http://eviltrout.com:8080/...` because the query compares against `eviltrout.com`. This makes such configured hosts fail closed and effectively unusable, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes for the wrong reason: it runs with no before-block, so SiteSetting.embed_truncate is still its default false (config/site_settings.yml line 'embed_truncate: false'), meaning expandable_first_post? returns false via the truncate check and the embeddable-host condition is never exercised. The test passes whether or not the code consults embeddable hosts at all — and indeed the new code (topic.rb line 869) removed the host check entirely, so the test name now describes behavior that no longer exists; a regression that re-adds or misimplements host gating (or drops truncate gating) would not be caught, and no test in the diff demonstrates the actual new behavior (true when embed_truncate? and has_topic_embed? hold with zero hosts fabricated).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb` `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks any embeddable-host setting (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the test `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` runs without setting `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` or stubbing `has_topic_embed?`, so it will return `false` due to default settings (not because hosts are blank). The surrounding tests also fabricate an `embeddable_host` in the “with an emeddable host” context, but since the method no longer consults hosts, those tests don’t exercise host-gating behavior either. This is a test correctness/coverage issue, not a runtime defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts the class hierarchy (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`) and never exercises create, update, or destroy. The new controller logic — params[:embeddable_host][:host]/[:category_id] extraction, the blank-category_id fallback to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 27-28), validation-failure rendering, and destroy of a nil host (line 17: `nil.destroy` raises NoMethodError when params[:id] doesn't match) — ships with zero behavioral assertions; any of these regressions passes CI green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Admin::EmbeddableHostsController with real behavioral risk/defects that are visible in code and untested. In `destroy`, it does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` followed by `host.destroy` with no nil guard; if the id doesn’t match a record, this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil.destroy`). The only new spec for this controller (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb) asserts class inheritance and does not exercise create/update/destroy paths, so these regressions would not be caught by CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddingController is a subclass check; neither show nor update is ever requested, and the update action's behavior (re-rendering the serializer with no persistence — embedding_controller.rb lines 11-13) is unverified. The admin embedding page's entire load path (OpenStruct model, EmbeddingSerializer with embed: :ids producing embeddable_host_ids that the new plural hydration in store.js must consume) and the saveChanges PUT round-trip have no test; a serializer key rename or route change passes CI and breaks the admin UI at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The pretender handler for GET /fruits/:id returns a hard-coded `fruits[0]` regardless of the requested id, and the store-test change to `store.find('fruit', 2)` (store-test.js.es6 lines 109-124) then asserts color ids 1,2 — which are apple's (fruits[0]) data, not banana's (color_ids [3]) — and never asserts `f.get('id')`. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the Pretender route `this.get('/fruits/:id', ...)` always returns `const fruit = fruits[0];` regardless of `:id` (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6). The updated test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are `[1,2]` (store-test.js.es6), which matches `fruits[0]` (apple) not the id=2 record (banana has `color_ids: [3]`). Since the handler ignores the requested id and the test never asserts `f.get('id')`, the test cannot actually validate per-id lookup/identity-map behavior and could mask regressions. This is a real, diff-grounded test/fixture quality issue rather than a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host_allowed? specs only use exact lowercase, port-free fixtures, while the validation regex on EmbeddableHost (embeddable_host.rb line 5) accepts hosts with a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and uppercase (//i), and before_validation strips neither ports nor case — but record_for_host compares `lower(host) = uri.host` (line 15), which excludes the port and is downcased. A host saved as 'Example.com:8080' or 'Example.com' passes validation and is persisted, yet host_allowed? can never match it ('example.com' ≠ 'example.com:8080' / stored case is not downcased before comparison), so the admin successfully adds a host that silently never allows embedding; the spec's fixture set (eviltrout.com, discourse.org) is exactly the input shape where this mismatch is invisible, so the defect ships covered-green.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `validates_format_of` regex allows an optional port `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not strip the port or normalize case. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (host without port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. If an admin saves a host containing a port (e.g. `Example.com:8080`), it can pass validation and be persisted with `:8080`, but lookups from referers like `http://example.com:8080/...` will query for `example.com` and never match the stored `example.com:8080`, so embedding will be silently disallowed. The specs only fabricate port-free lowercase hosts, so this mismatch wouldn’t be caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fabricator contents are swapped between files: category_fabricator.rb now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the :category/:diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category definitions. Tests still pass because Fabricate resolves by name across all fabricator files, but the file names now lie about their contents — the next contributor adding a category fabricator trait to category_fabricator.rb or a second embeddable_host definition (duplicate Fabricator name raises at load) gets bitten; this reads as a rename/move accident rather than intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `Fabricator(:category)` etc., and instead defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (with `category` association). Meanwhile the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. This mismatch between file names and contents is verifiable from the diff and is a maintainability/footgun issue (future contributors may add duplicate fabricators or look in the wrong file), but it doesn’t by itself introduce a runtime correctness defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guard `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is always false for a SELECT in PostgreSQL (PQcmdTuples returns 0 for SELECT statements), so the guarded INSERT block never runs, while the following `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` executes unconditionally. Every existing site's configured embeddable hosts are silently destroyed from site_settings with zero rows created in embeddable_hosts; after deploy, EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? returns false for all referers, breaking embedding site-wide (embed_controller/topic_retriever now depend on the table), and admins have no record of what hosts they had configured to re-enter.

adjudication.rationale: The migration does `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and guards on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` before reading `embeddable_hosts[0]['value']`. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that `cmd_tuples` is “always false” for a SELECT on PostgreSQL; `execute` returns a DB result object where `cmd_tuples` is commonly used as the row-count for SELECTs (i.e., 0 when no rows, 1 when one row). Therefore the claim that the INSERT block “never runs” and that hosts are “silently destroyed” cannot be concluded from the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `execute(...)[0]['id']` and `execute(...)[0]['value']` are indexed without a presence check, so when the first query returns no rows (embed_category setting absent, or its value not matching any category name exactly — e.g. the category was renamed or the setting stored an id), `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError instead of reaching the `if category_id == 0` uncategorized fallback that was written for exactly this case. The migration crashes mid-run on affected installs (table already created, transaction not clean), blocking the deploy; and because the CREATE TABLE is not recorded, any re-run hits the force: true drop path. The uncategorized fallback branch at lines 13-15 is dead code — the crash always happens first when the join is empty.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the join query returns at least one row. If it returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` missing, or its `value` doesn’t match any `categories.name`), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. The same unchecked `[0]['value']` pattern is used for the uncategorized id lookup. This is a real, diff-grounded migration-crash risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Host values from the free-text site_settings row are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no escaping or parameterization, so any previously configured host containing a single quote or other SQL-significant character produces a malformed statement. The migration raises a PG syntax error mid-migration (deploy blocker), aborting after the table has been created; even without quotes, the raw interpolation skips the escaping/parameterization the model layer would have applied. (Injection is Security's angle; the migration-crash data-integrity failure is this one.)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` directly interpolates each legacy host line into raw SQL: `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), this will produce invalid SQL and can abort the migration after creating the table. It also bypasses proper escaping/parameterization (and any model-layer normalization) when migrating existing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backfill INSERT bypasses the model's before_validation callback: raw setting values are stored as-is, so hosts saved with a protocol or path prefix (the old setting explicitly documented and accepted forms like 'http://discourse.org/1234' — see the removed embed_controller_spec fixtures) land in the host column unnormalized. Even once the cmd_tuples guard bug is fixed, every migrated host row containing 'http://' or a trailing path never matches `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, so the migrated hosts silently fail to allow embedding while appearing in the admin UI as if configured; a later admin edit of such a row would also fail the validates_format_of regex since the protocol was never stripped.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, legacy `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values are inserted via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) rather than through `EmbeddableHost`, so the model’s `before_validation` normalization (stripping `http(s)://` and paths) is bypassed. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` later parses the referer URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, which will not match rows stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`. This makes migrated hosts fail to allow embedding while appearing configured. Additionally, editing such rows later would hit `validates_format_of` which does not allow a protocol prefix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration is defined with `def change` but contains raw `execute` INSERT and DELETE statements that ActiveRecord cannot reverse, so `db:rollback` raises IrreversibleMigration, and the DELETE of the site_settings rows ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') destroys those values with no backup/export step. Once applied, the original configured host list and embed_category values cannot be recovered by rolling back the migration (rollback crashes, and even a manual down-migration has no source to restore from); combined with the dead cmd_tuples guard, the settings data is destroyed outright rather than migrated.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` is defined with `def change` but includes multiple raw `execute` statements (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE) and an explicit `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). In Rails, `execute` inside `change` is not automatically reversible, so `db:rollback` would raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` unless a `down`/`reversible` block is provided. However, the finding’s “data is destroyed outright rather than migrated” claim is overstated: the host list and category are read from `site_settings` and inserted into the new `embeddable_hosts` table before the delete, so the information is migrated (though not reversible back to the old settings representation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] delete() attaches only a .then to destroyRecord() with no .catch, so a failed DELETE (server error, session expiry, network drop) is swallowed as an unhandled rejection while save() on the same component routes failures to popupAjaxError. The admin clicks delete, confirms, and the row silently stays in the table with no error popup and no state change; the failure is invisible unless they happen to reload the page and see the host still present.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` without a `.catch(...)`, unlike `save()` which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE fails, the promise rejection is not handled here and no error UI is triggered, so the admin gets no feedback and the row will remain (since `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy looks the host up with .first and then unconditionally calls host.destroy, which raises NoMethodError on nil when the id does not exist, returning a 500 where a 404 belongs. A stale client (host deleted in another tab, or a retried delete after the first succeeded) gets a raw 500 instead of a 404/success; since the client UI has no catch, the deletion failure is also invisible to the user.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy` (and similarly `#update` passes a potentially-nil host into `save_host`). If the record doesn’t exist, `host` is `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response instead of a 404 or idempotent success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host] and assigns host.host on a possibly-nil record, so an update request with an unknown id (host = nil) or a request without the embeddable_host envelope crashes with NoMethodError and returns a 500 where a 4xx belongs. PUT /admin/embeddable-hosts/:id for a deleted id, or POST/PUT with a missing/malformed body, produces an unhandled 500 instead of 404/400; the client's popupAjaxError then surfaces a generic 'something went wrong' instead of a meaningful validation message.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`), so an unknown/deleted id will make `host` nil and raise `NoMethodError` (500). Separately, `save_host` also unconditionally dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` / `[:category_id]`, so a missing/malformed request body without the `embeddable_host` envelope will also raise `NoMethodError` (500) rather than returning a 4xx. (`#destroy` has the same nil-host risk: `host.destroy` without a nil check.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] record_for_host compares the stored host column (which the validation regex permits to contain a port like 'eviltrout.com:8080' and which before_validation never normalizes) against uri.host of the referer (which never contains a port), so any configured host entered with a port never matches and embedding is silently denied. An admin adds 'eviltrout.com:8080' via the new UI (it passes validation), but embed_controller#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever then reject every request from that host with Discourse::InvalidAccess — a regression from the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?, which stripped the port via URI(h).host before comparing; the admin sees the host listed as allowed while embedding fails with no diagnostic.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, validation explicitly allows an optional port in the stored `host` (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and path but does not strip the port. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, and `uri.host` never includes the port. So a stored value like `eviltrout.com:8080` (which can be saved via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host) will never match requests from `http://eviltrout.com:8080/...`, causing EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? (used in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) to reject embedding even though the admin configured it as allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with no rejection handler, and the server action it targets (Admin::EmbeddingController#update) persists nothing — it only re-serializes the fetched records. If this action is ever wired to a save button (its name and RESTful PUT route strongly suggest it), a failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection, and a success response falsely reports that changes were saved when the endpoint wrote nothing to the database; the actual persistence path is the per-host save() in the component, so the controller-level 'save' is a success-reporting no-op.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defining `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with no `.catch(...)`, and the corresponding server `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-serializes `@embedding` without persisting anything. However, the new `embedding.hbs` template does not wire any button/action to `saveChanges` (it only has per-host save/delete via the `embeddable-host` component and an `addHost` button), so there is no verifiable broken behavior in the UI as added here—it's more of a misleading/dead RESTful “save” endpoint/action that could cause unhandled rejections or no-op saves if later hooked up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] On save success the component sets host.category to Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId), but when the user leaves the category chooser empty the server coerces category_id to the uncategorized category while findById(null) yields undefined, so the client-side record diverges from the persisted row. The admin saves a host with no category chosen; the server stores the uncategorized category, but the row renders no category badge and the next edit() reads host.category.id as undefined, sending a blank category_id again — the displayed state never reflects what was actually saved, misdirecting any admin trying to verify the configuration.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6#save`, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and on success forces `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))`. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` coerces blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. If the chooser is left empty, `categoryId` is null/blank, so `findById(null)` yields `undefined` and the component sets `host.category` to `undefined`, while the persisted row has a real category_id. The template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, so it will show no category even though one was saved, and `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` which will be undefined and continue re-sending blank `category_id`.
